chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: Now, if you recall from the beginning of the lesson,

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: we talked about three major ways to estimate value.

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: One is intrinsic value, which we just covered.

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: Another is book value, which we're going to cover now.

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: And the other is market capitalization.

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: So let's take a look at book value.

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: Here's a classic definition of book value.

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: It's total assets of the company.

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: In other words, things like property that is owned and so on.

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: Minus intangible assets and liabilities.

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: So intangible assets are things that are difficult to put a price on.

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: They're things like the value of a brand or a patent or so on.

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: Liabilities are a little bit easier to calculate.

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: Those are just things like loans that are owed and so on.

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: So let's consider what is the book value for an example company.

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: Let's say the company owns four factories and

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: that each of these factories is worth about $10 million.

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: These are assets and altogether they're worth about $40 million.

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: Suppose this company also holds three very important patents and

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: each patent is valued at about $5 million.

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: The value of these patents is about $15 million.

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: But these are intangible assets that are hard to price exactly.

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: Finally, suppose this company has one large loan.

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: This would be under the liabilities column of $10 million.

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: If we follow this rule that book values total assets.

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: So total assets are this 40 million plus the 15 million or 55 million.

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: Minus intangible assets.

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: So we just don't count these intangible assets.

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: And liabilities.

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: So all together, we've got our total assets minus intangible assets,

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: which is 40 million.

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: And liabilities minus this 10 million.

chunks.title: Book value
chunks.text: So in this case, this company's book value is 30 million.
